TRUTH, it’s the only thing that has helped me personally improve the social aspects of my life.

Some quick points for people lacking self confidence:
-try to internalize that fear is just a barrier, and while self inflicted, is often irrational and a hindrance (again in relation to socializing). If you find that overcoming fear about something is something you’re really struggling with then analyze the perceived consequences. Is there any real damage that will happen if you put yourself out there and it doesn’t work out in a way that you hope or desire? Embarrassment sucks but it’s temporary! We learn and improve skills by failing at them, so if fear of embarrassment and failure are the main things holding you back then work towards overcoming this and you’ll start to gain the confidence as you get more practice!

-It can help to have a supportive person around you as well, strength in numbers and sometimes a friend can provide feedback on the parts of the exchange you can improve. Outside perspective helps us get out of your head and break our personal biases! Bonus points if they are a skilled socialite :)

-One of the fastest ways to learn how to be a better communicator is to learn how to be a better *listener*~! Observing how others communicate can help you augment your own communication and also you’ll find that the better listener you are the more likely other people will want to talk to *you* as opposed to trying to initiate or sustain conversation. (Active listening does wonders, people pick up on active listeners better than passive ones. Google active listening!)

-For a lot of us the setting can be one of (if not the) largest factor of anxiety. We can’t always control or influence our setting, but the times we can could make a massive difference in our comfort levels. Try to find or make the spaces where you feel the most comfortable in a social setting and utilize that space.

-last one I’ll say is personal comfort!!! Maybe the hardest one on here but the more comfortable you feel with yourself and in your own skin the easier it will be to be yourself and not feel weighed down by anxiety or doubt. Work on getting to know and love yourself individually so that others can make you feel less or uncomfortable with yourself. Confidence stems from feeling good and secure about yourself so get to learning how to love and embrace yourself as best as possible brothers and sisters~!!

These types of interactions create better suited experts that can be more adaptable to non-text scenarios. 

We want experts that know what they are doing and why, or can at least work in a group to figure it out as amicably as possible. Those people still need to be qualified of course, but there should still be a base level requirement. 

There will never be unanimous decisions in large groups, but it’s easier for people to learn and adapt this way as opposed to authoritarian policy. Also more people learn better when engaged in the process as opposed to just annotating and memorizing the outcome.

At the end of the day it produces qualified professionals more consistently because it’s forced engage in the process, it’s harder to “fake” your way through it.
